title: Domain Event Envelope
description: The envelope every domain event carries (backlog E1-013). Events are published through a transactional outbox, so consumers deduplicate on event_id and detect gaps with aggregate_version. An event carries identifiers and safe facts only: never evidence bytes, request bodies or secrets.

event_id.description: Idempotency key. A consumer that has seen this id must not act twice.

event_type.description: Carries its major version, so a removed or redefined field becomes a new type rather than a silent break.

aggregate_version.description: Ordering is guaranteed only within one aggregate. A consumer that sees a gap rebuilds from the source API rather than guessing.

causation_id.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for the first event in a chain.

payload.description: Fields declared for this event type in the catalog. Consumers ignore unknown optional fields, which is what makes an additive change backward compatible.

aggregate_type.description: Exactly one producer writes each aggregate type. Two writers would collide on aggregate_version or open gaps that consumers read as lost events.
